key_claims: Rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged adults carrying the high-risk APOE4 gene variant after four weeks of low-dose treatment.
Women carrying the APOE4 gene variant experienced the largest improvements in brain blood flow.
Participants without the APOE4 gene variant did not show the same improvement in brain blood flow from the treatment.
People carrying APOE4 can experience reduced brain blood flow years before noticeable memory difficulties begin.
limitations: The study did not establish whether the treatment could prevent Alzheimer's or preserve memory over time.
More research is needed to determine whether changes in brain blood flow lead to lasting improvements in brain health or a lower likelihood of developing the disease.
what_not_to_say: Rapamycin is proven to prevent or cure Alzheimer's disease.
The drug is recommended for all individuals at risk of cognitive decline without genetic screening.
